questions.question: Who among the following is the first Indian to get an Oscar Award?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following is the first Indian to get an Oscar Award?
questions.solution:
• At the 30th Academy Awards, Mehboob Khan's 1957 Hindi-language film Mother India was India's first submission for the Academy Award for the Best International Feature Film category.
    • It was nominated along with four other films and lost by one vote to the Italian film Knights of Cabiria (1957).
    • In 1982, the National Film Development Corporation of India was instrumental in co-producing the Richard Attenborough biographical film Gandhi.
    • Bhanu Athaiya became the first Indian to win an Academy Award for costume design at the 55th Academy Awards.
    • Ravi Shankar was nominated for Best Original Score for the same film. As of 2021, apart from Mother India, only two Indian films have been nominated for an Oscar – Salaam Bombay! (1988) and Lagaan (2001).
  • The Academy Awards, popularly known as the Oscars, are awards given for artistic and technical merit in the film industry.
    • First awarded May 16, 1929
    • Oscars 2021 Winners List
      • Best Picture: Nomadland
      • Best Actor: Anthony Hopkins – The Father
      • Best Actress: Frances McDormand – Nomadland

questions.question: Which playback singer was honoured with the Nightingale of Asia Award in 1987?
questions.questionHtml: Which playback singer was honoured with the Nightingale of Asia Award in 1987?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Asha Bhosle.

Key Points

  • Asha Bhosle is a renowned playback singer in India, known for her versatile voice and extensive career in the Indian music industry.
  • She has been honored with numerous awards and accolades, including the Nightingale of Asia Award in 1987.
  • Asha Bhosle is the sister of the legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar, and together, they have made significant contributions to Indian music.
  • Her career spans over seven decades, during which she has recorded songs for films, albums, and live performances, making her one of the most prolific singers in the world.

Additional Information

  • Playback Singing
    • Playback singing is a technique in Indian cinema where the singing voice is pre-recorded for use in movies, and the actors lip-sync to the songs on screen.
    • This practice allows for professional singers to provide high-quality vocal performances, while actors focus on their acting and on-screen presence.
  • Awards in the Music Industry
    • Music awards are given to recognize and honor achievements in the music industry, including performances, compositions, and contributions to the field.
    • Notable music awards include the Grammy Awards, the Academy Awards (Oscars) for Best Original Song, and national awards like the Filmfare Awards in India.
  • Contribution of Asha Bhosle
    • Asha Bhosle has sung in multiple languages, including Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and many more.
    • She is known for her versatility in singing various genres, including pop, classical, ghazals, and folk songs.
    • Her collaborations with music directors like R.D. Burman, O.P. Nayyar, and A.R. Rahman have resulted in some of the most iconic songs in Indian cinema.
  • The Nightingale of Asia Award
    • The Nightingale of Asia Award is an honor given to exceptional singers who have made significant contributions to the music industry in Asia.
    • It recognizes the impact and influence of the recipient's work on the music culture of the region.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first author writing in English to be conferred the Sahitya Akademi Award?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the first author writing in English to be conferred the Sahitya Akademi Award?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "RK Narayan".

Important Points

  •  R. K. Narayan was an Indian writer, who has written Malgudi days.
  • He becomes the main creator of early Indian literature in English in conjunction with Mulk Raj Anand and Raja Rao.
  • Some of his books are Swami and Friends, Bachelor of Arts, The English Teacher.
  • In 1960, he was awarded Sahitya Akademi Award for his novel The Guide.
  • R K Narayan awards with the AC Benson Medal from the Royal Society of Literature, the Padma Vibhushan and the Padma Bhushan, India's 2nd and 3rd maximum civilian awards, and in 1994 the Sahitya Akademi Fellowship, the best honor of India's countrywide academy of letters.
  • He becomes nominated to the Rajya Sabha, the higher residence of the Indian Parliament.

 

​Key Points

  • The Sahitya Academy Award is a literary honor in India.
  • The first awards were given in 1955.
  • The award amount was initially Rs 5,000, and has been gradually raised — it has been Rs 1 lakh since 2009. 
  • The Sahitya Akademi is India’s premier institution of letters, with a stated commitment to “promoting Indian literature throughout the world”.
  • The Akademi was established by Jawaharlal Nehru, who was also its first chairperson and inaugurated on March 12, 1954. 
  • Every year, the Akademi announces awards for authors of works of outstanding literary merit in Indian languages. Awards are currently given for 24 languages; the most recent additions being Bodo and Santhali in 2005.

questions.question: For which discovery did Henri Becquerel receive the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903?
questions.questionHtml: For which discovery did Henri Becquerel receive the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903?
questions.solution: Henri Becquerel received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 for his discovery of Spontaneous Radioactivity, sharing the prize with Marie and Pierre Curie for their work on radioactivity. His discovery, which was accidental, revealed that uranium salts emitted rays capable of exposing photographic plates without sunlight. This pivotal finding laid the foundation for the development of atomic physics and advanced the understanding of radioactive phenomena. Becquerel's work significantly contributed to future research in nuclear energy and medical diagnostics.

questions.question: Superconductivity was discovered by ______, who was also awarded the Noble Prize for Physics in 1913.
questions.questionHtml: Superconductivity was discovered by ______, who was also awarded the Noble Prize for Physics in 1913.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Heike Kamerlingh Onnes.

Key Points

  • Superconductivity was discovered in 1911 by the Dutch physicist Heike Kamerlingh Onnes, and he was awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1913 for his low-temperature research.
  • In 1908, Kamerlingh Onnes successfully liquefied helium. This allowed him to investigate the thermodynamics properties of helium in the liquid and gas phases.
  • He also investigated the electrical properties of metals down to about 1K.
  • In 1911, he observed the transition to a "zero resistance state" in a pure mercury sample as the temperature of the sample was lowered to below 4.2K.
  • He labeled this "zero resistance state" as "superconductivity."

Additional Information

  • Superconductivity:-
    • It is a complete disappearance of electrical resistance in various solids when they are cooled below a characteristic temperature. This temperature, called the transition temperature, varies for different materials but generally is below 20 K (−253 °C).
